newsitem.title: USA: Murdered rapper shoots to top of U.S. album charts.
newsitem.headline: Murdered rapper shoots to top of U.S. album charts.

text.p: Notorious B.I.G., the gangsta rapper who was gunned down last month, grabbed the No. 1 position on the U.S. music charts with his new album "Life After Death," his label said on Wednesday.

The double album sold almost 690,000 copies in the week ended March 30, and just over 6,000 copies the week before when some retailers violated its March 25 debut date, a common occurrence in the rap genre.

The album's official first week tally is the highest since the Beatles' double album "Anthology 1" debuted at the top of the charts with sales of 855,500 in November 1995. It also exceeds the first week sales of 664,000 for rival rapper Tupac Shakur's posthumous effort "Don Killuminati -- the Seven Day Theory" in November 1996.
Notorious B.I.G. recorded for New York-based Bad Boy Entertainment, whose albums are distributed by Arista Records, a unit of Germany's Bertelsmann AG.

His real name was Christopher Wallace, and he was also known as Biggie Smalls. He was murdered in a drive-by shooting as he was leaving a Los Angeles party in the early hours of March 9. No one has been apprehended for the killing.
"Life After Death," Smalls' second album, features the oversize rapper on the cover standing next to a hearse. The songs include "Somebody's Gotta Die" and "You're Nobody (Til Somebody Kills You)."
